/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 14 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2667 (-134)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3630 (-364)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2409 (-23)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1845 (12)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1003 (3)
CAPESIZE
The downward pressure continued today, with both the Pacific and Atlantic contributing to further losses in the Capesize market. The BCI 182 5TC fell by $3,302 to $32,920, while the C5 index dropped by $0.930 to $12.050 and the C3 index declined by $1.070 to $31.610. In the Pacific, despite two C5 miners being active, the market came under further pressure. Offers were initially heard in the mid $13s but quickly retreated as the bid was reported at $11.70. Bids gradually improved, resulting in a number of fixtures by one miner around the $12.10 level. The second miner appeared content to observe, with offers reportedly in the high $12s but little indication of a willingness to engage at those levels. Conditions in the Atlantic deteriorated further, with activity remaining very limited and sentiment continuing to weaken. C3 was fixed at $31.50 for 10 November onwards, while better bids for end-November lay in the low $33s against offers closer to $34. The North Atlantic also softened, with a weaker transatlantic fixture contributing to a $5,246 decline in the C8 index. With both basins losing ground and limited signs of resistance emerging, sentiment across the Capesize market remains firmly on the defensive.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic slipped further today, outweighing the gains seen in the Pacific, with the P5TC falling by $206 to $21,680. Both trans-Atlantic and fronthaul activity were described as active however, market sources suggested sentiment remains negative as fundamentals continue to shift towards an oversupply of tonnage, particularly off the North Continent. As a result, the bid-offer spread is widening as charterers are said to test lower levels, with a lack of grain demand for fronthaul also being highlighted. The Pacific is described as remaining the more upbeat basin, supported by healthy demand from Australia, which is helping to sustain positive sentiment and maintain fixing levels. Market sources also reported active Indonesian coal exports, while period activity remained evident, particularly for laden legs and short period employment.

Atlantic
The Ultra Cougar (81,922 2015) open Jorf Lasfar 16 October was said to have been placed on subjects for a trans-Atlantic round, with some suggesting to Glencore. The Sargas (82,167 2026) open Ijmuiden 20/21 October was reported to have fixed, but no other information surfaced.

Asia
The MP Kamsarmax 1 (81,190 2017) open Cai Lan 19 October was reported fixed for a trip from Australia to India. The Syrma (82,111 2025) open Hitachinaka 20/21 October fixed an EC Australia trip to India at a rate reportedly in the region of $25,000-$26,000. The MG Kronos (84,790 2016) open Fukuyama 19 October fixed from EC Australia for redelivery Singapore-Japan range at around $26,000, although the charterer was not reported.
SUPRAMAX
Another steady if unexciting day, with the 11TC average up $156 to $23,327. The North Pacific continues to throw up some strong numbers with the tonnage list said to be limited, with a newbuilding open Japan reportedly on subjects with Pacific Basin for a trip via NoPac to Salalah at close to $27,000 and Hyundai Glovis linked to another newbuilding ex yard North China for a backhaul to the Mediterranean at $29,250. Further south rates remain steady for the shorter trips back to China, but trips to India have nudged up as the Indian Ocean appears flat. In the Atlantic the Continent and Mediterranean both appeared steady, although a source said there was a softer undertone on certain routes in the Mediterranean and fewer scrap cargoes in the market from the Continent, whilst the US Gulf has seen more activity and rates have recovered slightly. Further south it looked positional with the bigger units doing better, with a 63,000-dwt fixed from Rio Grande via Santos to Ain Sukhna intention sugar with redelivery Port Said at $36,000, whilst there were differing opinions of fronthaul levels.
HANDYSIZE
The market delivered a mixed performance, with some regions holding steady or edging lower, while others recorded gains ranging from modest to strong. The BHSI edged up by 3 points to 1,003, while the 7TC average rose by $62 to $18,056. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, only marginal adjustments were observed, with rates remaining largely unchanged. The South Atlantic remained balanced and keep showing positive movement. In the US Gulf, sentiment was more muted, as an extended tonnage list continued to weigh on rates. Meanwhile, the Asian market experienced a generally active day, with favourable conditions and sentiment continuing on a positive trajectory. On the period side, a 37,000-dwt vessel open China 20–25 October was fixed for 3–5 months at $16,000, with worldwide redelivery, although further details were not disclosed.

Atlantic
The Nordic Oslo (35,853 dwt, built 2012) was placed on subjects for a trip from Santos to the west coast of South America at $31,500, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
A 37,000-dwt open Singapore was fixed for two to three laden legs at $18,000, with the first trip to the US West Coast. Meanwhile, a 38,000-dwt open West Australia was placed on subjects for an outbound trip at close to the mid-$20,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Rio Tinto Q3 Results

In its latest quarterly earnings release, Rio Tinto reported a 0.7 Mt year-on-year decline in Australian iron ore production (100% basis) to 83.4 Mt in 3Q26. Meanwhile, sales rose 1.3 Mt to 85.7 Mt, on steady mine output and well-stocked ports, and a shift towards lower grade exports. Year-to-September sales climbed 8.4 Mt to 243.3 Mt, with Pilbara iron ore sales guidance remains unchanged at 323-338 Mt, in line with last year’s sales of 326.2 Mt. According to the report, higher diesel prices due to geopolitical tensions have added $0.9/t to unit cash costs year-on-year YTD.
